b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Country They Belonged To
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited a museum about the new republics, and she asks what country people felt part of after independence.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.prompt: Tell Meg about the country people belonged to.
cues: Say that the country was new
Use a relative clause with a preposition
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.target: El país al que pertenecían era nuevo.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.english: The country they belonged to was new.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-01.canDo: I can use *el que*, *la que*, *los que* and *las que* after a preposition to describe the country or community people belonged to.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Mexican Anthem
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.scenario: You are Meg. You are preparing a class about national symbols, and Carlos asks about the Mexican anthem.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.prompt: Tell Carlos when the Mexican anthem was first sung.
cues: Say what was sung, with se
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.target: El himno mexicano se cantó por primera vez en 1854.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.english: The Mexican anthem was sung for the first time in 1854.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-02.canDo: I can use the passive with *se* (*se crearon himnos*) to say what was created and when.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Historians Say Is Important
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg watched a documentary about Mexico's symbols, and she asks what historians say today.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.prompt: Tell Meg what is important, according to historians.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.target: Es importante que se estudie la vida real de las comunidades.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.english: It is important that the real life of the communities is studied.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-03.canDo: I can use the subjunctive after value judgments (*es importante que*, *es necesario que*) to say what historians think matters.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Borders and Families
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.scenario: You are Meg. You read a book about the borders of the Andes, and Carlos asks what happened to families.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what families did although there was a border.
cues: Say that there was a border, with aunque
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.target: Aunque había una frontera, muchas familias seguían juntas.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.english: Although there was a border, many families stayed together.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-04.canDo: I can use *aunque* to contrast what a border said with what people did.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Heroes in the History Books
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you how the history books of the 19th century presented the heroes of independence.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.prompt: Tell Meg how the heroes were presented.
cues: Say how they were presented, with ser and a participle
Say that they were fathers of the nation
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.target: Los héroes fueron presentados como padres de la patria.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.english: The heroes were presented as fathers of the nation.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-05.canDo: I can use the passive with *ser* (*fueron presentados como padres de la patria*) to say how heroes and books were presented.

b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Nation
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are preparing for a class, and he asks what the new republics created after independence.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what was created after independence.
cues: Say what was created, with se
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.target: Después de la independencia se crearon banderas y himnos.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.english: After independence flags and anthems were created.
b1-nacionnacionalismo-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the nation with relative clauses with a preposition, the passive with *se*, the subjunctive after value judgments, *aunque* and the passive with *ser*.
